verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              धृतराष्ट्रं ततः सर्वे ददृशुर्जनमेजय। पृष्ट्वा सुखमथो राज्ञः पृष्टा राज्ञा च भारत॥१॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said : O Janamejaya, O descendant of Bharata, then they all saw Dhritarashtra and asked his welfare; they were also asked their welfare in reiurn,

verses.sanskrit: ततस्तैर्विहितः पूर्वं समङ्गो नाम बल्लवः। समीपस्थास्तदा गावो धृतराष्ट्रे न्यवेदयत्॥२॥
verses.english: Then a cowherd named Samanga who had been instructed before-hand come to the king Dhritarashtra and spoke about the cattle.

verses.sanskrit: अनन्तरं च राधेयः शकुनिश्च विशाम्पते। आहतुः पार्थिवश्रेष्ठं धृतराष्ट्रं जनाधिपम्॥३॥
verses.english: O king, the son of Radha (Karna) and Shakuni thus spoke to that foremost of kings, the ruler of earth, Dhritarashtra,

verses.sanskrit: रमणीयेषु देशेषु घोषाः सम्प्रति कौरव। स्मारणे समयः प्राप्तो वत्सानामपि चाङ्कनम्॥४॥
verses.english: "O descendant of Kuru, our cattle are now stationed in a charming place. The time for marking the calves has also come.

verses.sanskrit: मृगया चोचिता राजन्नस्मिन् काले सुतस्य ते। दुर्योधनस्य गमनं समनुज्ञातुमर्हसि॥५॥
verses.english: O king, this is also an excellent season for your son Duryodhana to go to a hunting expedition. Therefore you should grant him permission to go there.

verses.sanskrit:
धृतराष्ट्र उवाच।
              मृगया शोभना तात गवां हि समवेक्षणम्। विश्रम्भस्तु न गन्तव्यो वल्लवानामिति स्मरे॥५॥
verses.english: O king, this is also an excellent season for your son Duryodhana to go to a hunting expedition. Therefore you should grant him permission to go there.

verses.sanskrit: ते तु तत्र नरव्याघ्राः समीप इति नः श्रुतम्। अतो नाभ्यनुजानामि गमनं तत्र वः स्वयम्॥७॥
verses.english: But I have heard that those foremost of men (the Pandavas) are living some where near that place; therefore I think you should not yourselves go there.

verses.sanskrit: छद्मना निर्जितास्ते तु कार्शिताश्च महावने। तपोनित्याश्च राधेय समर्थाश्च महारथाः॥८॥
verses.english: Defeated by deceitful means, they are now living in the deep forest in great misery. O son of Radha, those greatly powerful car-warriors are now engaged in asceticism.

verses.sanskrit: धर्मराजो न सङ्क्रुद्ध्येद्भीमसेनस्त्वमर्पणः। यज्ञसेनस्य दुहिता तेज एव तु केवलम्॥९॥
verses.english: Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira) will never be angry, but Bhimasena is naturally wrathful; the daughter of Yajnasena (Draupadi) also is effulgence herself.

verses.sanskrit: यूयं चाप्यपराध्येयुर्दर्पमोहसमन्विताः। ततो विनिर्दहेयुस्ते तपसा हि समन्विताः॥१०॥
verses.english: Full of pride and folly as you are you are certain to give her offence. Endued with ascetic merit as she is (now), she will certainly consume you.

verses.sanskrit: अथवा सायुधा वीरा मन्युनाऽभिपरिप्लुताः। सहिता बद्धनिस्त्रिंशा दहेयुः शस्त्रतेजसा॥११॥
verses.english: Or perhaps, those heroes, armed with swords and other weapons and filled with wrath, may consume you with the fire of their weapons.

verses.sanskrit: अथ यूयं बहुत्वात्तानभियात कथञ्चन। अनार्यं परमं तत् स्यादशक्यं तच्च वै मतम्॥१२॥
verses.english: Or if from the force of numbers you seek to injure them in any way, even that will be a highly improper act, though I know you will never succeed.

verses.sanskrit: उषितो हि महाबाहुरिन्द्रलोके धनञ्जयः। दिव्यान्यस्त्राण्यवाप्याथ ततः प्रत्यागतो वनम्॥१३॥
verses.english: The mighty armed Dhananjaya (Arjuna) had lived in the abode of Indra. Having obtained the celestials weapons, he has returned to the forest.

verses.sanskrit: अकृतास्त्रेण पृथिवी जिता बीभत्सुना पुरा। किं पुनः स कृतास्त्रोऽद्य न हन्याद्वो महारथः॥१४॥
verses.english: While unaccomplished in arms, Bibhatsu (Arjuna) conquered the whole earth. He is now a great car-warrior and highly accomplished in arms, why will he not be able (now) to kill you all?

verses.sanskrit: अथवा मद्वचः श्रुत्वा तत्र यत्ता भविष्यथ। उद्विग्नवासो विश्रम्भाद्दुःखं तत्र भविष्यति॥१५॥
verses.english: Or if you in obedience to my words on going there, behave carefully you will then never be able to live happily, as you will always be in a state of trustlessness.

verses.sanskrit: अथवा सैनिकाः केचिदपकुर्युर्युधिष्ठिरम्। तदबुद्धिकृतं कर्म दोषमुत्पादयेच्च वः॥१६॥
verses.english: Or some soldiers of yours may do some injury to Yudhishthira and that unpremeditated act may be ascribed to you. O descendant of Bharata, therefore let some faithful men go there to count the cattle and mark the calves. I do not think it is proper for your to go in person.
verses.bhavadeepa: उद्विग्नवास इति वनवासेनोद्विग्नेषु पाण्डवेषु विश्रम्भात् सत्यव्रता एते नास्मान् बाधिष्यन्त इति विश्वासाद्यो भवतां वासः स दुःखं दुःखदो भविष्यति । पूर्वापकृते विश्वासो न कर्तव्य इत्यर्थः ॥१५॥

verses.sanskrit: तस्माद्गच्छन्तु पुरुषाः स्मारणायाप्तकारिणः। न स्वयं तत्र गमनं रोचये तव भारत॥१७॥
शकुनिरुवाच। धर्मज्ञः पाण्डवो ज्येष्ठः प्रतिज्ञातं च संसदि। तेन द्वादश वर्षाणि वस्तव्यानीति भारत॥१८॥
verses.english: Shakuni said: O descendant of Bharata, the eldest Pandava is virtuous; he has taken the pledge in the assembly that he will live twelve years in the forest.

verses.sanskrit: अनुवृत्ताश्च ते सर्वे पाण्डवा धर्मचारिणः। युधिंष्ठिरस्तु कौन्तेयो न नः कोपं करिष्यति॥१९॥
verses.english: The other Pandavas are virtuous and obedient to him. The son of Kunti, Yudhishthira will never be angry with us.

verses.sanskrit: मृगयां चैव नो गन्तुमिच्छा संवर्तते भृशम्। स्मारणं तु चिकीर्षामो न तु पाण्डवदर्शनम्॥२०॥
verses.english: We desire very much to go to a hunting expedition; we shall also take that opportunity to count the cattle. We have no wish to see the Pandavas.

verses.sanskrit: न चानार्यसमाचारः कश्चित् तत्र भविष्यति। न च तत्र गमिष्यामो यत्र तेषां प्रतिश्रयः॥२१॥
verses.english: We shall not go to that place where the Pandavas are living. Therefore no misconduct on our part can possibly arise.

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              एवमुक्तः शकुनिना धृतराष्ट्रो जनेश्वरः। दुर्योधनं सहामात्यमनुजज्ञे न कामतः॥२२॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said : Having been thus addressed by Shakuni, the ruler of earth, Dhritarashtra, unwillingly gave permission to Duryodhana and his counsellors togo.

verses.sanskrit: अनुज्ञातस्तु गान्धारिः कर्णेन सहितस्तदा। निर्ययौ भरतश्रेष्ठो बलेन महता वृतः॥२३॥
verses.english: Having received permission, the son of Gandhari, that foremost of the Bharata race (Duryodhana) with Karna and with a large host started.

verses.sanskrit: दुःशासनेन च तथा सौबलेन च धीमता। संवृतो भ्रातृभिश्चान्यैः स्त्रीभिश्चापि सहस्रशः॥२४॥
verses.english: He has accompanied by Dushasana the intclligent son of Subala (Shakuni) and by many others of his brothers and also thousands of women.

verses.sanskrit: तं निर्यान्तं महाबाहुं द्रष्टुं द्वैतवनं सरः। पौराश्चानुययुः सर्वे सहदारा वनं च तत्॥२५॥
verses.english: When he started to see that lake in the Dvaitavana, the citizens also with their wives proceeded towards that forest.

verses.sanskrit: अष्टौ रथसहस्त्राणि त्रीणि नागायुतानि च। पत्तयो बहुसाहस्रा हयाश्च नवतिः शताः॥२६॥
verses.english: Eight thousand cars, thirty thousand elephants, nine thousand horses and many thousands of foot soldiers,

verses.sanskrit: शकटापणवेशाश्च वणिजो बन्दिनस्तथा। नराश्च मृगयाशीलाः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥२७॥
verses.english: Carriages, shops, pavilions, traders, bards and men, trained in hunting, by hundred and thousands, followed the king.

verses.sanskrit: ततः प्रयाणे नृपतेः सुमहानभवत् स्वनः। प्रावृषीव महावायोरुद्धतस्य विशाम्पते॥२८॥
verses.english: O monarch, as the king started, followed by many thousands of men, the uproar caused by the march resembled the deep roar of winds in the rains.
verses.bhavadeepa: शकटाः भारवाहान्यनांसि । आपणाः पण्यानि । वेशो वेश्याजनाश्रयः ॥२७॥

verses.sanskrit: गव्यूतिमात्रे न्यवसद्राजा दुर्योधनस्तदा। प्रयातो वाहनैः सर्वैस्ततो द्वैतवनं सरः॥२९॥
verses.english: Arriving at the lake of Dvaitavana with his followers and conveyances, king Duryodhana encamped at the distance of four miles from the lake.
